import pytest
from rich.cells import split_text, split_graphemes, _split_text
from rich.segment import Segment
from rich.style import Style


def test_split_text_at_column_zero():
    """Test splitting text at column zero returns empty left and full text right."""
    result = split_text("hello", 0)
    assert result == ("", "hello")


def test_split_text_at_column_zero_with_wide_chars():
    """Test splitting mixed single and double-cell text at column zero."""
    # Using some wide characters
    result = split_text("你好", 0)
    assert result == ("", "你好")


def test_split_text_at_column_zero_single_cell_only():
    """Test splitting single-cell-only text at column zero."""
    result = split_text("abc", 0)
    assert result == ("", "abc")


def test_split_text_at_column_zero_empty_string():
    """Test splitting empty string at column zero."""
    result = split_text("", 0)
    assert result == ("", "")


def test_split_text_positive_position():
    """Test that positive positions still work (regression test)."""
    result = split_text("hello", 2)
    assert result == ("he", "llo")


def test_split_text_at_end():
    """Test splitting at or past end still works."""
    result = split_text("hello", 5)
    assert result == ("hello", "")
    
    result = split_text("hello", 10)
    assert result == ("hello", "")


def test_split_text_middle_position():
    """Test splitting in the middle works."""
    result = split_text("abcdef", 3)
    assert result == ("abc", "def")


def test_split_text_with_double_cell_middle():
    """Test splitting where a double-cell char gets replaced with spaces."""
    # This is harder to test without knowing exact wide chars
    # but the behavior should be: if we cut into a 2-cell char, 
    # it becomes two spaces
    text = "a你b"  # a (1-cell) + 你 (2-cell) + b (1-cell)
    # Cell positions: a=0-1, 你=1-3, b=3-4
    # Splitting at position 2 should cut the 你 in half
    result = split_text(text, 2)
    assert result[0][-1] == " "  # Should end with space
    assert result[1][0] == " "   # Should start with space

import pytest
from rich.segment import Segment
from rich.style import Style


def test_segment_split_cells_at_zero():
    """Test splitting segment at column zero."""
    segment = Segment("hello")
    left, right = segment.split_cells(0)
    assert left.text == ""
    assert right.text == "hello"


def test_segment_split_cells_at_zero_with_style():
    """Test splitting styled segment at column zero preserves style."""
    style = Style(bold=True)
    segment = Segment("hello", style=style)
    left, right = segment.split_cells(0)
    assert left.text == ""
    assert left.style == style
    assert right.text == "hello"
    assert right.style == style


def test_segment_split_cells_positive():
    """Test splitting segment at positive position works."""
    segment = Segment("hello")
    left, right = segment.split_cells(2)
    assert left.text == "he"
    assert right.text == "llo"


def test_segment_split_cells_at_end():
    """Test splitting segment at or past end."""
    segment = Segment("hello")
    left, right = segment.split_cells(5)
    assert left.text == "hello"
    assert right.text == ""
    
    left, right = segment.split_cells(10)
    assert left.text == "hello"
    assert right.text == ""


def test_segment_split_cells_middle():
    """Test splitting segment in the middle."""
    segment = Segment("abcdef")
    left, right = segment.split_cells(3)
    assert left.text == "abc"
    assert right.text == "def"


def test_segment_split_cells_zero_empty():
    """Test splitting empty segment at zero."""
    segment = Segment("")
    left, right = segment.split_cells(0)
    assert left.text == ""
    assert right.text == ""


def test_segment_split_cells_with_control():
    """Test splitting segment with control codes."""
    # Control segments should maintain their properties
    segment = Segment("hello", control=(("test",),))
    left, right = segment.split_cells(2)
    # The behavior with control segments is that split_cells still works
    assert left.text == "he"
    assert right.text == "llo"

    assert result == ("", "hello")

    """Test internal _split_text with various positive positions."""
    text = "hello world"
    result = _split_text(text, 5)
    assert result == ("hello", " world")

import pytest
from rich.cells import split_graphemes


def test_split_graphemes_basic():
    """Test split_graphemes basic functionality."""
    spans, total_width = split_graphemes("hello")
    assert total_width == 5
    assert len(spans) == 5
    # Each span should be (start, end, width)
    assert spans[0] == (0, 1, 1)
    assert spans[4] == (4, 5, 1)


def test_split_graphemes_empty():
    """Test split_graphemes with empty string."""
    spans, total_width = split_graphemes("")
    assert total_width == 0
    assert spans == []


def test_split_graphemes_wide_chars():
    """Test split_graphemes with wide characters."""
    spans, total_width = split_graphemes("a你b")
    # a is 1 cell, 你 is 2 cells, b is 1 cell = 4 total
    assert total_width == 4
    assert len(spans) == 3


def test_split_graphemes_with_unicode_version():
    """Test split_graphemes respects unicode_version parameter."""
    spans, total_width = split_graphemes("hello", unicode_version="auto")
    assert total_width == 5
    # Should not raise
    assert len(spans) > 0

import pytest
from rich.cells import chop_cells


def test_chop_cells_basic():
    """Test chop_cells basic functionality."""
    result = chop_cells("hello world", 5)
    assert len(result) >= 1
    # Each chunk should fit within width
    for chunk in result:
        from rich.cells import cell_len
        assert cell_len(chunk) <= 5


def test_chop_cells_empty():
    """Test chop_cells with empty string."""
    result = chop_cells("", 5)
    assert result == []


def test_chop_cells_single_line():
    """Test chop_cells where text fits in one line."""
    result = chop_cells("hi", 5)
    assert len(result) == 1
    assert result[0] == "hi"


def test_chop_cells_exact_fit():
    """Test chop_cells where text exactly fits width."""
    result = chop_cells("hello", 5)
    # "hello" is 5 cells, should fit
    chunks = [c for c in result if c]
    assert all(len(c) > 0 for c in chunks)


def test_chop_cells_narrow_width():
    """Test chop_cells with very narrow width."""
    result = chop_cells("hello", 1)
    # Should have 5 chunks of 1 char each
    assert len(result) == 5
